answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a oasis as the anchor of the cost. A beacon stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a prism holds...
